definitions.explanation: The number seven. Like four, seven has two readings: なな and しち. なな is more commonly used in everyday counting because しち can be confused with いち (one) or し (four) when spoken.

examples.japanese: {七|なな}{時|じ}に{会|あ}いましょう。
{一|いっ}{週間|しゅうかん}は{七|なな}{日|にち}です。
{七|なな}{月|がつ}に{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.english: I'm going to Japan in July.
examples.notes: しちがつ is also correct

examples.japanese: {七|しち}{月|がつ}は{夏|なつ}の{始|はじ}まりで、{毎日|まいにち}とても{暑|あつ}くなります。
examples.english: July is the beginning of summer, and it gets very hot every day.
examples.notes: {七|しち}{月|がつ} uses the しち reading

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}{七|なな}{時|じ}に{起|お}きて、{顔|かお}を{洗|あら}ってから{朝|あさ}ごはんを{食|た}べます。それから{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}きます。
examples.english: I wake up at seven in the morning, wash my face, and then eat breakfast. Then I go to school.

notes:
{七|なな} has two readings: なな (native Japanese) and しち (Sino-Japanese). なな is preferred in most spoken contexts because しち can be confused with {一|いち} (one) or {四|し} (four).

WHEN TO USE EACH READING:
- なな: safer in most situations, especially when counting aloud
- しち: used in set expressions like {七|しち}{月|がつ} (July), {七|しち}{五|ご}{三|さん} (Shichi-Go-San festival)
- Either: {七|なな/しち}{時|じ} (seven o'clock) — both are common

COUNTER COMBINATIONS:
- {七|なな}つ: seven things (native counter)
- {七|なな}{人|にん}: seven people
- {七|なな}{本|ほん}: seven long objects
- {七|なな}{冊|さつ}: seven books
- {七|なな}{百|ひゃく}: seven hundred

CULTURAL:
- {七|しち}{五|ご}{三|さん}: festival celebrating children aged 7, 5, and 3 (November 15)
- {七|しち}{福神|ふくじん}: the Seven Lucky Gods
- {七夕|たなばた}: Star Festival (July 7th — note the special reading)
